A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIA-Bench and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained experiments and illustrations can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 29 MLLMs on MIA-Bench, supervised fine-tuning results, judge comparisons, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations across judge versions and a mixed-data fine-tuning experiment.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, weighted sub-instruction scoring, grading prompt, and supervised fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. The expanded weighting explanation and DIT terminology clarify existing procedures; the new data-mixture experiment introduces no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Section 3.2 adds LLaVA Visual Instruct 150K as an additional training corpus mixed with the existing 5,000 generated instruction pairs. The 400-pair benchmark, its image sources, and its instruction categories remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4o to the cross-benchmark comparison, expanding its comparator set from five to six models. v4 Tables 4–5 add a mixed-data SFT control. Table 1 retains all 29 models; Gemini-Pro/Gemini-1.0-Pro and Reka/Reka-Core are naming clarifications.

E3.justification: v4 adds four specified judge-version conditions for an eight-model comparison and a mixed-data SFT condition. The original scoring protocol and one-epoch DIT training remain. The added comparison has a model-size ambiguity: Table 3 labels LLaVA-1.5-13b, whereas Appendix Tables 7–9 label the corresponding entries LLaVA-1.5-7b.

E4.justification: The original two-model Claude-3-Opus judging check is substantially extended with cross-version judge sensitivity across eight models, including category-level results in Appendix A.3. A new training-data ablation tests whether adding LLaVA-Instruct150K helps. The IFEval analysis is retained and relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement that multiple evaluation runs may vary by approximately 1%. Neither specifies run counts or seeds, or adds confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new judge comparisons do not change statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial judge-dependent results in Tables 3 and 6–9 and mixed-data SFT results in Tables 4–5, including a MIA-Bench score of 78.90. Table 2 gains GPT-4o and revised rankings. All 29 Table 1 score rows and retained DIT-only results are unchanged; the SFT MathVista results of 33.0 and 32.0 disappear.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The sub-instruction weighting and score normalization rules remain unchanged; v4 adds explanatory rationale rather than new mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a 400-pair benchmark for precise multimodal instruction adherence, comparative model evaluation, and improvement through additional SFT. The abstract's claim of avoiding performance compromise on other tasks is also retained.

C2.justification: v4 explains weighting through instruction importance and difficulty, interprets the added judge comparisons as showing stable rankings, and concludes that mixing in LLaVA-Instruct150K provides no further improvement. The existing limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises future open-sourcing; v4 supplies a benchmark/evaluation-code repository address and an explicit release statement. The added judge study names specific model versions. These improve documented access and configuration information, without adding a detailed SFT implementation recipe.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited research works, and positioning against IFEval, InfoBench, and multimodal benchmarks remain substantively unchanged. Citation-style changes, added bibliographic URLs, and metadata updates do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 expands the scoring explanation, Section 3.2 introduces DIT terminology, and a reproducibility statement is added. The appendix organization changes after moving the IFEval comparison into the main text. Most existing narrative and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the empirical displays: Table 1 groups models by size, comparison and SFT tables gain rows, and five judge-comparison tables are added. Figure 2 is redrawn with a different MMMU example, and the existing IFEval plot moves into the main text. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: The broader judge-sensitivity study, mixed-data SFT control, and explicit benchmark/code access information modestly improve validation and reproducibility. Benefits are tempered by inconsistent LLaVA-7B/13B labels, an unqualified ranking-consistency claim despite the LLaVA/ShareGPT4V rank swap, and limited discussion of the mixed-data model's transfer regressions in Table 5.
